---
title: Graph and geometry
---

Atom i of a graph is atom i of its geometry. Every routine crosses between the two: it
seeds a structure from the graph, and checks each structure it gets back against the graph.

Geometries are autogeom's `Geometry`, which carries `charge` and `spin` too.

## Seeding a structure

`embed` runs RDKit's ETKDG on a Lewis structure of the graph, with its determined LS as
constraints, and keeps its atom order, charge and spin. Reading the structure back gives
the same graph:

```python
>>> import autogeom as ag
>>> import protomol as pm
>>> smg = pm.examples.species()
>>> geo = pm.embed(smg)
>>> isinstance(geo, ag.Geometry), geo.symbols == list(smg.symbols)
(True, True)
>>> pm.from_geometry(geo) == smg
True

```

## Checking a structure

A conformer search or an optimization can invert a centre, flip a bond or break one. A
structure is kept only if it is still the workflow's graph. `geometry_mismatches` perceives
the bonds from covalent radii, as `from_geometry` does, and reads each determined LS's
parity from the coordinates. All three fields empty means they agree, and the result is
false, like an empty container:

```python
>>> pm.geometry_mismatches(smg, geo)
GeometryMismatches(missing_bonds=(), extra_bonds=(), reacting_bonds=(), stereo=())
>>> bool(pm.geometry_mismatches(smg, geo))
False

```

Each disagreement names its atoms: a bond as a pair, an LS by its site (the centre, or a
bond's end pair). The (1S, 3Z) stereoisomer's structure contradicts both LS of the (1R, 3E)
graph:

```python
>>> other = pm.embed(pm.from_smiles(r"C[C@H](O)/C=C\C"))
>>> pm.geometry_mismatches(smg, other).stereo
(1, (3, 4))

```

An LS the coordinates don't decide (a flat centre, a double bond twisted by about 90°) is
not a mismatch, and neither is an undetermined one. On a reaction graph, only the bonds
that neither break nor form and the LS that don't change are compared, so the end points
of an IRC and the TS all agree with it (see [Reaction coordinate](03-reaction.qmd)).

## Perceiving a graph

For a structure from outside a workflow (an INCITE geometry, an IRC end point), the atom
order is kept. The LS sites are the low-T ones `from_smiles` gives, and every parity is
read from the coordinates, so the graph describes this structure atom for atom:

```python
>>> geo = ag.from_smiles(r"C[C@@H](O)/C=C/C")  # stands in for an outside structure
>>> gra = pm.from_geometry(geo)
>>> gra.symbols[:5], (gra.charge, gra.spin), pm.is_determined(gra)
(('C', 'C', 'O', 'C', 'C'), (0, 0), True)
>>> pm.canonical_json(gra) == pm.canonical_json(pm.examples.species())
True
>>> pm.display(gra, atom_indices=True)  # doctest: +SKIP

```

Renumbering the geometry renumbers the graph the same way. A mirror-image structure gives
the enantiomer:

```python
>>> mirror = pm.from_geometry(ag.reflect(geo, [0.0, 0.0, 1.0]))
>>> pm.canonical_json(mirror) == pm.canonical_json(pm.from_smiles(r"C[C@H](O)/C=C/C"))
True

```
